items.title: Billy Taylor interviewed by Michael Woods, New York City, New York, July 27, 1995
items.q: my Uncle Bob was really the catalyst for my interest. He gave me my first Fats Waller record, he gave me my first Art Tatum record, and he introduced me to a lot of the local pianists

ctx.x: Let me just ask you some opening questions. You — literally you are a history of jazz. I mean you know so much about this music. I wanted to ask you, let’s start chronologically and kind of move up. What attracted you to playing the piano and who were some of the other keyboard artists at the time that you started that kind of got you into the music?

Well usually I answer that question by saying that I had an uncle who was my father’s brother, everyone on my father’s side played the piano. But this one uncle played jazz as opposed to European classical music, which everybody else played in my grandfather’s church. So my Uncle Bob was really the catalyst for my interest. He gave me my first Fats Waller record, he gave me my first Art Tatum record, and he introduced me to a lot of the local pianists, many of whom were really terrific. And he knew everybody. And…
And how did you first start working professionally?
